bridges.pageIntent: Invite expert falsification and a bounded teaching experiment around Boundary-First Chess, not endorsement of the wider theory.

hero.title: You already make chess legible at speed. I built a structural language I want you to try to break.
hero.support: Boundary-First Chess reframes positions through constrained possibility, reachable states, pressure, closure, defect, repair, and decision geometry.

bridges.executiveBrief: The smallest useful collaboration is one game, position family, or teaching theme analyzed in both ordinary chess language and the Boundary-First vocabulary to see whether the added structure helps, confuses, or says nothing new.
bridges.whyYou: The page is aimed at a high-volume chess educator and communicator capable of testing whether a new explanatory representation survives contact with real positions and real learners.

bridge.theirWorld: Fast, accessible chess explanation has to preserve strategic structure without drowning the learner in engine output or specialist vocabulary.
bridge.bflMachinery: A complete Boundary-First Chess manuscript and a mechanics vocabulary for possibility, pressure, boundary, closure, defect, repair, and promotion.
bridge.intersection: Use the framework as an additional teaching instrument on a bounded set of positions and compare what it makes easier or harder to see.

proof.claimBoundary: No endorsement or instructional superiority is assumed. Negative critique is useful evidence.

collaboration.ask: Choose one position, game, or concept and try to break the representation.

closing.primary: Let's put it on a board.
